program_meta.program_name: PhD in Computer Science, Department of Computer Science (College of Science), Purdue University West Lafayette. Alternate route: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering, Elmore Family School of ECE (separate major within the same Purdue graduate application). MS options: MS in Computer Science (thesis and non-thesis; thesis-vs-non-thesis is NOT chosen at application time), joint Statistics-Computer Science MS (select area of interest 'CS/Stat (MS only)' in the portal), and BS/MS 4+1 (Purdue undergrads only).
program_meta.sop_limit: CONFLICTING GUIDANCE - resolve before writing. (1) Purdue CS Statement of Purpose page, VERBATIM: 'There is no word limit but it is in your best interest to be concise.' The same page asks for a structured document: 'We prefer that you write a comment or short paragraph under each of the following headings and upload into the electronic application system: Applicant's Name: / Long Term Degree Objective: / Research Experience: / Publications: / Future Research Interests: / Other Comments:'. (2) Purdue CS Application FAQ, VERBATIM: 'There is no specific word limit for the Academic Statement of Purpose and the Personal History Statement. We recommend staying within 300-500 words.' (3) Purdue OGSPS (Graduate School) how-to-apply page, VERBATIM: 'A statement, not exceeding two pages in length, is encouraged.' NET EFFECT: CS is the reviewing body and asks for 300-500 words in a headed format - dramatically shorter than the 1000-word norm used for other schools on this list. A separate short, structured Purdue version of the SOP is required.
program_meta.extra_essays: TWO extra items beyond the SOP. (1) Personal History Statement - required by OGSPS of all applicants, uploaded separately; no stated word limit (CS FAQ recommends the same 300-500 words; OGSPS says 'The Academic Statement of Purpose and the Personal History Statement are two of the most important documents in your graduate application. The documents should be concise'). Required prompts, VERBATIM: 'Describe how your background and life experiences contribute to your ability to be both persistent and resourceful in your graduate studies. Describe how your life experiences have prepared you to contribute to an academic community where scholars with diverse research interests, abilities, backgrounds, and experiences are supported, respected, and valued.' Optional prompt covers mitigating factors in the academic record. (2) CS Supplementary Form (PDF) - a CS-specific coursework form listing program courses/textbooks; FAQ says 'The CS Supplemental Form is for the Grad Admissions Committee to gain a better understanding of your overall program courses.' A resume/CV is also a required upload.
program_meta.deadline_fall_2027: December 1, 2026 for Fall 2027 start (MS and PhD, Purdue CS). Verbatim from the CS Application Steps page: 'Fall 2027 start-December 1, 2026'. Submission and fee payment due by 11:59:59 p.m. EST on that date (OGSPS rule). No priority deadline: 'The graduate program in Computer Science does not utilize a priority application deadline at this time.' Decisions for the Fall cohort are released Feb./Mar.; offers sent prior to April 15. (Spring 2027 alternative deadline is October 1, 2026.)
program_meta.lor_count: Three (3). Purdue CS Letters of Recommendation page, VERBATIM: 'At least three letters of recommendation must be submitted electronically as part of your Electronic Graduate School application before the application deadline.' Also: 'If you have done research, we expect a recommendation from your supervisor.' and 'Not waiving your right to review a letter of recommendation tends to diminish the value of the letter.' OGSPS default is also three unless a program states otherwise. If applying to two majors on one application, the program requiring the most letters sets the minimum; a single letter addressing both programs is acceptable.
program_meta.gre: NOT REQUIRED. Purdue CS Requirements page, VERBATIM: 'GRE is NOT required.' CS FAQ, VERBATIM: 'GRE scores are not required by the CS Admissions Committee.' GRE is not an OGSPS requirement either, though some other Purdue programs require it - confirm separately if also applying to ECE.
program_meta.english_test: REQUIRED FOR AKSHAT - INDIA IS NOT EXEMPT. Purdue's only country-based waiver is the 'Waiver - Citizen of or Degree from English Speaking Country', and the published list of official English-speaking countries does NOT include India (list includes Australia, Canada, Ghana, Kenya, New Zealand, Nigeria, Philippines, Singapore, South Africa, UK, etc.). CS FAQ confirms no exceptions: 'If the minimum scores are not met, the Purdue Graduate School will not make exceptions.' OGSPS MINIMUMS: TOEFL iBT overall 80 with Writing 18 / Speaking 18 / Listening 14 / Reading 19 (for exams taken before 21 Jan 2026); for exams on or after 21 Jan 2026 the new scale requires overall 4.0 with Writing 4.0 / Speaking 3.5 / Listening 3.5 / Reading 4.0. IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with Reading 6.5 / Listening 6.0 / Speaking 6.0 / Writing 5.5. Duolingo overall 115 with all four integrated subscores 115. CS COMPETITIVE BAR (higher than the university minimum): 'While we consider a TOEFL score of 100 with sub scores no less than 22 to be competitive...'; IELTS 7.5; and for Duolingo 'CS expects to see an overall score of no less than 135 with no sub-score less than 135.' Duolingo is accepted for graduate admission only, not for GTA eligibility. Scores valid two years and must be valid at time of admission. Purdue does NOT accept TOEFL MyBest scores or the IELTS One Skill Retake. Purdue institution code for score reports: 1631.
program_meta.app_fee: $75 USD for international applicants ($60 for domestic). One fee covers up to two campus and/or major selections on the same application. Purdue CS does NOT grant fee waivers for international applicants: 'Due to the overwhelming number of nomination and application fee waiver requests received in Computer Science, we are unable to provide waivers or accept nominations.' International payment available via Flywire.
program_meta.faculty_directory_url: https://www.cs.purdue.edu/people/faculty/index.html (CS, filterable by research area; 'Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing' is the relevant filter); https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/People/Faculty (ECE); https://ipai.research.purdue.edu/directory/ (Institute for Physical AI affiliates)
program_meta.advisor_model: DEPARTMENT ADMISSION, NOT ADVISOR ADMISSION. Purdue CS FAQ asks and answers this directly, VERBATIM: 'Do I need to secure a faculty advisor before admission? No, there is no need to secure a faculty advisor prior to admission.' Applications are reviewed by the CS Grad Admissions Committee holistically; an advisor is found after arrival. PhD admits are automatically considered for fellowships/TAships/RAships with no separate funding application. Naming faculty in the SOP is still expected - the OGSPS SOP guidance says 'Identify faculty who share your research and scholarly interests. Reviewers will want to know that you have researched the program, faculty, and key focus areas.' Purdue's application allows up to TWO campuses and/or majors on one application and one fee, so CS (1st choice) + ECE (2nd choice) is possible - but only ONE Academic Statement of Purpose and ONE Personal History Statement are submitted, and OGSPS requires that they be 'all-inclusive' and support suitability for BOTH programs. Selectivity: 'For Fall 2024 we received over 3900 applications for PhD and MS combined and admitted around 290.'
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, with caveats. The CS MS has a thesis option (thesis vs non-thesis is decided after enrolment, not at application). CS FAQ, VERBATIM: 'Admitted MS students who pass the core requirements of the doctoral program and show strong potential for research with a CS faculty member may petition to join the PhD program. Interested students should explore this possibility by conducting research (ideally two semesters) with a CS faculty member.' PhD students may earn the MS concurrently. Funding warning: 'MS applicants may be considered for funding during the application process. However, they typically do not receive an offer at admission. Once on campus, many find assistantships in CS or other departments.' The department also states it 'prefers grad students who have the desire and potential to receive a PhD.' Several faculty here (Ruqi Zhang, Rajiv Khanna) explicitly list MS students as welcome in the lab.
program_meta.notes: COMPETITIVE PROFILE: CS states 'Most of the successful applicants have major and cumulative GPAs above 3.5/4.0, 8.5/10.0 or 85/100. We take the quality of the institution into consideration.' Akshat's 9.56/10 clears this comfortably. First-year PhD stipend quoted (2023-24 rate) $23,389 academic year / $31,390.50 with summer. CONTACT CHANNEL RULE, VERBATIM and repeated on three CS pages: 'Please note that all communications regarding potential admission need to be sent to csgradinfo@purdue.edu. Messages sent to other emails or through other channels will not receive a response.' This governs ADMINISTRATIVE questions; it does not appear to bar research emails to individual faculty, several of whom explicitly invite them (Khanna, Ruqi Zhang, Kihara). CS also states: 'We do not hold open house events for the graduate program in Computer Science' and 'Due to the large capacity of inquiries and questions, we do not offer phone or virtual sessions.' TRANSCRIPTS: unofficial transcripts are now accepted for review and admission; Purdue does NOT accept WES credential evaluations. INSTITUTE FOR PHYSICAL AI (IPAI): launched Dec 2025, $20M from the Lilly Endowment, 250+ faculty affiliates, 20+ affiliated centers; Director is Ananth Grama (Samuel D. Conte Distinguished Professor of CS). IPAI is a research institute, not a degree-granting unit - PhD admission still runs through CS or ECE. IPAI runs a postdoctoral fellows program (relevant later, not now). faculty.lab: Not separately named; group page at ruqizhang.github.io/#group (6 PhD students, 1 postdoc). Office DSAI 3097.
faculty.research_areas: Scalable, reliable and efficient probabilistic methods for ML and generative AI. Three stated directions: (1) alignment and safety of foundation models including diffusion models; (2) probabilistic inference, uncertainty estimation and Bayesian methods; (3) generation and learning on discrete data. Also gradient-based discrete sampling, SG-MCMC, calibration, long-tailed classification, low-precision sampling.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's spine-MRI semi-supervised study is fundamentally a calibration question: he compared confidence thresholding against MC-dropout uncertainty for filtering pseudo-labels, found combining them adds nothing, and showed per-class thresholds calibrated on 5 reference images match those derived from 304 - i.e. that the uncertainty signal used to select data is cheap to calibrate. Zhang's 'Rethinking Data Distillation: Do Not Overlook Calibration' (ICCV 2023) makes the mirror-image argument on the data side: models trained on distilled/synthetic data are badly miscalibrated and standard post-hoc calibration fails on them. Akshat's A-PDF work (scoring cWGAN-GP-generated masks against the class-proportion distribution of real masks instead of trusting the discriminator) is exactly the kind of synthetic-data-quality-control problem her calibration + probabilistic-modelling machinery is built for, and 'CoT-UQ: Improving Response-wise Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs with Chain-of-Thought' (ACL Findings 2025) shows she is still actively building uncertainty estimators intended to be used as filters. Her diffusion line (CANDI, ICML 2026) also connects to his DDPM-pretraining work.
faculty.key_paper_1: Rethinking Data Distillation: Do Not Overlook Calibration. ICCV, 2023.
faculty.key_paper_2: CANDI: Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Diffusion Models. ICML, 2026. (See also: CoT-UQ: Improving Response-wise Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs with Chain-of-Thought, Findings of ACL 2025; Making Reliable and Flexible Decisions in Long-tailed Classification, TMLR 2025.)
faculty.taking_students: Yes. Homepage states she is looking for PhD, MS, undergrad and intern students; no date on the notice, but the news feed is current to 6/2026 (NVIDIA Academic Grant) and she is co-chairing the Midwest Machine Learning Symposium at Purdue in Summer 2026, so the lab is clearly active and funded (NSF IIS RI 2025, Amazon Research Award 2025, Biomolecular Design Seed Grant 2/2026). Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: VERBATIM: 'I am looking for highly motivated students (PhD, MS, undergrads, and interns) to join our lab. If you are interested, feel free to reach out.' No further screening instructions, no required attachments, no 'do not email' language.
faculty.email_angle: I ran the negative-result version of your ICCV 2023 calibration argument on the label side - MC-dropout uncertainty and confidence thresholding gave the same pseudo-label quality on spine MRI, and combining them added nothing - and I would like to work on what actually makes an uncertainty signal useful as a data filter.
faculty.notes: Best combination at Purdue of (a) genuine topical overlap with interests A and B, (b) an unambiguous open door, and (c) CS-department home so a single CS application reaches her. Caveat: her 2025-2026 output has tilted heavily toward LLM/VLM alignment and safety - the uncertainty/calibration thread is real but is currently being applied to language models rather than images. Frame the pitch around the METHOD (uncertainty as a selection mechanism), not the medical domain.

faculty.lab: Not separately named; group of ~7 PhD students listed at raymond-yeh.com/#people
faculty.research_areas: Machine learning and computer vision: generative and perceptual models, equivariance and symmetry with formal guarantees, ML safety (model immunization, unlearning, distillation detection), out-of-distribution and anomaly detection, structured/optimization layers in deep nets.
faculty.why_match: HiME's whole claim is that hierarchy consistency is a THEOREM, not a measurement - per-level conditional sigmoids composed by the chain rule give an upward-closed prediction set by construction, at ~0.01% parameter overhead and verified across five backbones. Yeh builds exactly this class of result for a different symmetry: 'Group Downsampling with Equivariant Anti-aliasing' (ICLR 2025) and 'Truly Scale-Equivariant Deep Nets with Fourier Layers' (NeurIPS 2023) make equivariance hold by construction rather than by augmentation, and 'Tunable Soft Equivariance with Guarantees' (CVPR 2026) asks the follow-on question Akshat's Table V raises - what does the structural constraint COST when the encoder is weak, and how should the constraint be relaxed? Separately, 'Not All Unlabeled Data are Equal: Learning to Weight Data in Semi-supervised Learning' (NeurIPS 2020) is a learned version of the hand-tuned per-class pseudo-label thresholds Akshat used to lift a spine-MRI student from 0.735 to 0.816 mIoU, and 'Moving Alphabet: A Controlled Study of Training Data for Text-to-Video Generation' (2026) is the same controlled-ablation methodology Akshat used to isolate preprocessing gains in the polyp study.
faculty.key_paper_1: Group Downsampling with Equivariant Anti-aliasing. ICLR, 2025.
faculty.key_paper_2: Tunable Soft Equivariance with Guarantees. CVPR, 2026. (See also: Truly Scale-Equivariant Deep Nets with Fourier Layers, NeurIPS 2023; Not All Unlabeled Data are Equal: Learning to Weight Data in Semi-supervised Learning, NeurIPS 2020.)
faculty.taking_students: Yes - and he names the exact cycle. Homepage 'To prospective students' block states openings for Ph.D. starting Fall 2027. NSF CAREER Award June 2026; Google Research Scholar 2025; NSF IIS RI 2024. Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: Not stated - no emailing instructions of any kind on the site. The only prospective-student text is, VERBATIM: 'To prospective students. We are looking for highly motivated and talented students! Openings for Ph.D. (Fall 2027) and Undergrad at Purdue with the intention to pursue graduate school.' Email address is published in obfuscated form ('rayyeh at purdue dot edu'), which usually signals email is acceptable but unsolicited volume is unwelcome - keep it to a few sentences.
faculty.email: rayyeh@purdue.edu (published on homepage as 'rayyeh at purdue dot edu')
faculty.email_angle: Your Fourier-layer and group-downsampling work makes equivariance hold by construction; I built the hierarchical analogue - a chain-rule decoding rule that makes taxonomy consistency a theorem at 0.01% parameter overhead - and my own ablation shows the constraint is free under a fine-tuned encoder but costs accuracy under a frozen one, which is the question your 'tunable soft equivariance' paper is asking.
faculty.notes: Sharpest METHODOLOGICAL match at Purdue for HiME (interest C) and the one faculty member who explicitly names Fall 2027 as the recruiting cycle. Domain mismatch to be honest about: he does no medical imaging - the shared ground is guarantees-by-construction and controlled empirical study, not the application area. Also an ML-safety/unlearning line that Akshat has no history in.

faculty.lab: Not separately named; research programme described under 'Constraint Reasoning Embedded in Machine Learning' (CORE) and 'AI-driven Scientific Discovery' on his homepage. NSF CAREER awardee.
faculty.research_areas: Integration of automated/constraint reasoning with machine learning; structured prediction under hard constraints; probabilistic inference and discrete integration (XOR/parity constraints, probabilistic circuits); symbolic regression and AI for scientific discovery; constrained generative models.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's HiME establishes hierarchy consistency by construction - the decoding rule itself guarantees an upward-closed prediction set over 37 classes and 4 levels of the Galaxy Zoo 2 taxonomy, at 95.8% decision-level accuracy. Xue's 'Constraint Reasoning Embedded Structured Prediction' (JMLR 23(345), 2022) is the direct precedent for that design pattern: CORE embeds decision diagrams as a fully differentiable module so that, in his own words, 'the structures generated with CORE satisfy 100% of the constraints when using exact decision diagrams' and constraint satisfaction also shrinks the modelling space and improves learning. His 'Embedding Decision Diagrams into Generative Adversarial Networks' (CPAIOR 2019) is the generative counterpart to Akshat's A-PDF, which filters cWGAN-GP samples against the class-proportion distribution of real masks - Xue would frame that post-hoc filter as a constraint that should be compiled into the generator instead. The thread is still live: 'Solving Satisfiability Modulo Counting Exactly with Probabilistic Circuits' (ICML 2025) and he taught CS 592 'Automated Reasoning and Machine Learning Integration' in Spring 2026.
faculty.key_paper_1: Constraint Reasoning Embedded Structured Prediction. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 23(345):1-40, 2022.
faculty.key_paper_2: Solving Satisfiability Modulo Counting Exactly with Probabilistic Circuits. ICML, 2025. (See also: Embedding Decision Diagrams into Generative Adversarial Networks, CPAIOR 2019; Sequential Prediction with Logic Constraints for Surgical Robotic Activity Recognition, RO-MAN 2021.)
faculty.scholar: not found on his homepage (no Google Scholar link published; full publication list is maintained on the homepage itself)
faculty.taking_students: Unstated. No prospective-student notice anywhere on the site. Indirect evidence of an active, funded group: NSF CAREER award (NSF #2339844), multiple 2025-2026 papers with current PhD students (Nan Jiang, Jinzhao Li, Daniel Xie, Maxwell Jacobson), and CS 243 scheduled for Fall 2026. Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: not stated. Homepage publishes only 'Email: yexiang AT purdue DOT edu' and 'Tel: (765) 496-0456' with no instructions, no screening requirements and no do-not-contact notice.
faculty.email: yexiang@purdue.edu (published on homepage as 'yexiang AT purdue DOT edu')
faculty.email_angle: CORE gets 100% constraint satisfaction by embedding exact decision diagrams; I got 100% hierarchy consistency by a much cheaper route - chain-rule composition of per-level conditional sigmoids, ~38K parameters - and I would like to understand where that cheap trick stops working and a real reasoning module becomes necessary.
faculty.notes: The single closest intellectual collision with HiME anywhere in this file. Two honest caveats. (1) DRIFT: the flagship constraint-embedded-structured-prediction papers are 2019-2022; his 2024-2026 output is dominated by symbolic regression, materials/nuclear-physics discovery, and LLM literature analysis, plus a burn-wound imaging collaboration with Juan Wachs (IE). The constraint+ML thread continues but through solvers and probabilistic circuits rather than deep structured prediction. (2) His group is heavily symbolic/discrete-optimisation flavoured; Akshat has no background in decision diagrams, SAT/SMT or probabilistic circuits, so this is a genuine retooling, not a continuation. Note also his 'Same-Decision Probability: A Confidence Measure for Threshold-Based Decisions' (IJAR 2012) - an early link to Akshat's threshold-calibration result.

faculty.rank: Professor (full professor since 2024); Chair of the CNSIP area in ECE; Deputy Editor-in-Chief, IEEE Transactions on Computational Imaging
faculty.department: Elmore Family School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, with a courtesy appointment in the Department of Statistics
faculty.research_areas: Computational imaging: co-design of sensors and algorithms. Diffusion and flow models as image priors, generative photography, photon-limited / quanta image sensor imaging, single-photon LiDAR, imaging through atmospheric turbulence, plug-and-play priors, robust machine learning. Author of the widely used 'Tutorial on Diffusion Models for Imaging and Vision' (arXiv:2403.18103).
faculty.why_match: Akshat's DDPM result is that a diffusion encoder pretrained on unlabelled abdominal CT lifts liver Dice from 0.751 to 0.928 and that a FROZEN encoder retains 87% of that - but the same frozen encoder fails below random init on kidney, and he wants to know why a learned prior transfers for one structure and not another. Chan's 'Why Fine-grained Labels in Pretraining Benefit Generalization?' (TMLR 2024) is a direct attack on that exact question - it isolates what property of the pretraining signal makes the learned representation transfer - and 'Kernel Diffusion: An Alternate Approach to Blind Deconvolution' (ECCV 2024) plus 'FlowSteer: Conditioning Flow Field for Consistent Image Restoration' (CVPR 2026) are the same 'diffusion/flow as a prior over images' machinery Akshat used, applied where the forward model is known. Secondary hook: i2Lab's single-photon LiDAR line ('Resolution Limit of Single-Photon LiDAR', CVPR 2024) maps onto Akshat's Perception Lead role doing LiDAR-camera fusion on the autonomous go-kart.
faculty.key_paper_1: Why Fine-grained Labels in Pretraining Benefit Generalization? Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 2024.
faculty.key_paper_2: Tutorial on Diffusion Models for Imaging and Vision. arXiv:2403.18103, 2024. (See also: Kernel Diffusion: An Alternate Approach to Blind Deconvolution, ECCV 2024; FlowSteer: Conditioning Flow Field for Consistent Image Restoration, CVPR 2026.)
faculty.taking_students: NO - explicit. i2Lab Opportunities page, VERBATIM: 'Graduate Research Assistant(s): (2026-2027) As of May 2026, we do not have openings for RA.' The page nevertheless keeps a full 'we are interested in students who meet these criteria' section and email instructions, so the notice may be revised before the Dec 1 2026 deadline. Lab funding remains heavy (NSF CCSS 2025-2027, NSF CIF 2025-2027, DARPA CIDAR 2025-2026, DARPA-SRC JUMP 2.0 2023-2027, Samsung GRO 2023/24/25). Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: VERBATIM (graduate section): 'If you are interested, please send Prof. Chan an email with the following items: Your resume / CV; Transcript; One representative paper (e.g., a journal article, a conference paper, or a project report). Tips: Read carefully about what we do in i2Lab, and convince us that you can contribute.' The same page lists hard prerequisites, VERBATIM in part: 'I expect incoming students have self-learned this course: Fourier Optics Lectures on YouTube', plus linear algebra (MIT 18.06 / Purdue MA 511), probability and statistics (MIT 18.05 / Purdue ECE 302), convex optimization (Stanford EE 364a / Purdue ECE 647), machine learning theory (Caltech Learning from Data / Purdue ECE 595), 'Adequate programming skills: PyTorch, TensorFlow', 'Independence: Can solve problems by yourself', 'Good English: Speaks well. Writes well.'
faculty.email: not listed on the lab site as a plain address (the Opportunities page instructs applicants to email him but does not print the address); Purdue ECE directory format is stanchan@purdue.edu - verify on the ECE directory before sending
faculty.email_angle: Your TMLR paper on why fine-grained pretraining labels help generalization is the question my own diffusion-pretraining result forced on me: the frozen encoder kept 87% of fine-tuned liver Dice but fell below random initialisation on kidney, and I have no principled account of the difference.
faculty.notes: RED FLAG, decisive for timing: 'As of May 2026, we do not have openings for RA' for 2026-2027. Listed Close on research fit, not on availability - re-check the Opportunities page in October/November 2026 before naming him as the primary target. SECOND STRUCTURAL ISSUE: he is ECE, not CS. A CS-only application will not route to him. Purdue's single application permits two majors, so CS + ECE is the mechanism - but that forces one shared, 'all-inclusive' SOP across both, which is hard to do well in the 300-500 words CS recommends. THIRD: his prerequisite list (Fourier optics, convex optimization, ML theory) is the most demanding of anyone here and is optics-heavy; Akshat has none of the optics background. If contacting, the resume + transcript + one representative paper package is mandatory, not optional.

faculty.department: Department of Computer Science (joined Spring 2022). Office DSAI 3112. Affiliated with IPAI.
faculty.lab: Not separately named; group page at rjvak7.github.io/group
faculty.research_areas: Foundational machine learning: data-efficient learning (coresets, data pruning, spectral sparsifiers), subset selection theory, optimization and learning dynamics (SAM vs SGD, simplicity bias), machine unlearning and memorization, human-AI systems and learning from subjective annotations.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's polyp study held the architecture fixed and varied only preprocessing across three backbones, and found that the data-side gain shrinks as the architecture strengthens (+0.058 on U-Net down to +0.023 on Attention U-Net) - an empirical statement that data can substitute for representational capacity, up to a point. Khanna's entire 'Data-efficient learning' thrust is the formal version of that question, and 'Stable Coresets via Posterior Sampling: Aligning Induced and Full Loss Landscapes' (arXiv:2511.17399, 2025) states the criterion Akshat's pseudo-label filter was groping for by hand: a data subset should preserve not just first-order statistics but gradients, curvature and the shape of the full-data loss landscape. That is a principled replacement for the per-class confidence thresholds that took his spine-MRI student from 0.735 to 0.816 mIoU. 'Spectral Valleys and Sharp Failures in Greedy Determinant Maximization' (COLT 2026) supplies the failure-mode analysis - when greedy selection provably breaks - which is the kind of negative result Akshat already writes.
faculty.key_paper_1: Spectral Valleys and Sharp Failures in Greedy Determinant Maximization. COLT (PMLR v336), 2026.
faculty.key_paper_2: Stable Coresets via Posterior Sampling: Aligning Induced and Full Loss Landscapes. arXiv:2511.17399, 2025. (See also: A Unified Stability Analysis of SAM vs SGD: Role of Data Coherence and Emergence of Simplicity Bias, arXiv:2511.17378, 2025; Sharpness-Aware Machine Unlearning, arXiv:2506.13715, 2025.)
faculty.taking_students: Yes - the most explicit at Purdue. Homepage, VERBATIM: 'I have multiple PhD positions available.' Also advertising Fall 2026 postdoc positions at IPAI. Verified 2026-08-28.
faculty.contact_policy: VERBATIM: 'If you are interested in working with me, please send me a note before you apply.' This is an instruction to email BEFORE submitting the application, which makes him the single most time-sensitive contact on this list given the December 1, 2026 deadline.
faculty.email_angle: Your stable-coresets criterion - preserve the shape of the loss landscape, not just first-order statistics - is what I was approximating badly by hand when I tuned per-class confidence thresholds to filter pseudo-labels on 54 labelled spine MRIs.
faculty.notes: Listed Partial rather than Close only because the overlap is at the level of the QUESTION (which data matters, and why) rather than the setting - his work is theory-and-optimization-first (COLT, spectral analysis, loss-landscape geometry), with no images, no segmentation and no semi-supervised pipelines. Akshat would need substantially more optimization theory than he currently has. That said: highest actionability of anyone at Purdue - multiple funded PhD slots AND a verbatim instruction to make contact before applying. Treat the pre-application email as a to-do item, not an option. IIT Bombay MTech, so he will read an Indian undergraduate transcript accurately.

faculty.department: Department of Computer Science. Office 3121 DSAI.
faculty.lab: Not named; statistical learning theory group. Program Committee Chair (with Tor Lattimore) for COLT 2026.
faculty.research_areas: Statistical learning theory: theoretical foundations of active learning, universal learning rates, sample complexity of PAC and multiclass learning, sample compression, transfer and multitask learning, adversarially robust and semi-supervised learnability, bandit feedback.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's central empirical claim in the spine-MRI work is that a teacher trained on 54 labelled images, used to generate filtered pseudo-labels, produces a student at 0.816 mIoU - +8.1 points over the teacher - i.e. that selective use of unlabelled data beats passive use of the labelled set. Hanneke's 'Agnostic Active Learning Is Always Better Than Passive Learning' (NeurIPS 2025, Oral) is the theorem-shaped version of precisely that claim, and it is his most recent flagship result, not a legacy interest. 'Data Selection for ERMs' (COLT 2025) formalises the question Akshat answered empirically when he showed thresholds calibrated on 5 reference images match those from 304 - how few examples are needed to fix a selection rule. 'A Characterization of Semi-Supervised Adversarially-Robust PAC Learnability' (NeurIPS 2022) is the semi-supervised bridge.

faculty.why_match: Akshat's DDPM work and his nucleus-segmentation work are both about extracting structure from noisy 3D/2D biomedical volumes where dense annotation is unaffordable; his A-PDF contribution specifically is a post-hoc SCORER that decides which generated outputs to trust. His DiffModeler / CryoZeta / DMcloud tools are diffusion-based modelling from density maps, which is the structural-biology analogue of Akshat's diffusion-pretraining-then-segment pipeline on abdominal CT.
